answer.rationale: memory_57 rates lowest (2) because referral incentives target established customers and revenue addition without retention harm, but provide no evidence about long-term sustainability, repeat revenue quality, or margin impact—the core drivers of sustainable long-term qualified revenue. memory_73 (3) is weakly supported because promotional pricing can drive acquisition volume but may attract low-lifetime-value accounts and obscure true willingness-to-pay, creating revenue that appears strong short-term but may not be durable. memory_86, memory_91, and memory_31 (all 4) directly improve activation, engagement, and early product adoption—foundational to sustainable revenue by increasing customer lifetime value and reducing churn risk. memory_44 (5) most directly supports the objective: enterprise deals through sales-assisted flows signal higher deal quality, longer contract terms, lower churn, and measurably better pipeline durability than self-serve, making it the strongest proxy for sustainable long-term qualified revenue.
